# Test fixtures

Hand-built PDF files committed as bytes, so `cargo test` proves the reader
against real file structure without any external tool (no `qpdf`, `verapdf`,
`mutool`, `pdfinfo` or `gs` is installed here).

Rules for every file in this directory:

- Small and reviewable. Text-only fixtures can be read in an editor. The files
  containing Flate-compressed streams are byte-for-byte reproducible:
  `python3 tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py` rebuilds them, and running it twice
  must not change a single byte (`md5` the directory to check).
- Self-describing: a fixture only contains what the test that loads it asserts.
  The file name says what structure it exercises.
- Byte-stable: never regenerated by a script during `cargo test`; a change to a
  fixture is a deliberate commit.
- Paired with an assertion: every fixture has at least one test naming it, and
  the test says which clause (see `docs/SPEC-MAP.md`) it is proving.

## Files

| File | Structure | Loaded by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classic-xref.pdf` | `%PDF-2.0`, catalog/pages/page in one classic table, then an incremental update that adds a content stream and repaints page 3 with the `/Resources` that stream needs | `tests/document.rs`, `tests/cli.rs` |
| `classic-twin.pdf` | the same object graph as `xref-stream.pdf`, written with a classic table | `tests/xref_streams.rs`, `tests/content.rs` |
| `xref-stream.pdf` | cross-reference is a `/Type /XRef` stream; objects 1–3 sit in `/ObjStm` 5, object 4 is a plain stream | `tests/xref_streams.rs` |
| `xref-stream-prev.pdf` | same file plus an incremental update: object 4 replaced, second xref stream with `/Prev` | `tests/xref_streams.rs` |
| `hybrid-xref.pdf` | classic table for the plain objects plus a trailer `/XRefStm` hiding objects 1–3 | `tests/xref_streams.rs` |
| `text.pdf` | one page whose `/Contents` is **uncompressed** and walks through `Tj`, `TJ` with a gap adjustment, `'`, `TL`/`T*`, `Tm`, two fonts (WinAnsiEncoding and a `/Differences` array) | `tests/content.rs` |
| `encrypted-r6.pdf` | the object graph of `plain-twin.pdf` with `/V 5 /R 6` AES-256: catalog string, content stream and metadata stream encrypted; `/Encrypt` carries `/U`, `/O`, `/UE`, `/OE`, `/Perms`. User password `user`, owner password `owner` | `tests/encryption.rs` |
| `plain-twin.pdf` | the same document in the clear, for text comparison | `tests/encryption.rs` |
| `page-tree.pdf` | three pages (5, 6, 7) under a nested tree: root `/MediaBox` + `/Resources`, node `/Rotate 90`, page overrides for `/MediaBox`, `/CropBox` and `/Rotate`, plus an XMP `/Metadata` stream | `tests/pages.rs` |

Seven of the plain fixtures are produced by `tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py`,
which computes every offset (and compresses the streams with `zlib`, the same
DEFLATE format `flate2` reads), so the fixtures do not depend on any PDF
library. They stay small enough to read in an editor: `classic-xref.pdf` in
particular is plain ASCII with its offsets visible in the table.

The encryption pair comes from `cargo run --example make_encrypted_fixture`
(`examples/make_encrypted_fixture.rs`): no `qpdf`, `mutool` or `gs` is installed
here, so an R6 file has to be generated in-repo. Its salts, IVs and "random"
bytes are fixed, and `md5` shows the files are reproduced exactly.
